B1:
Touched fires many times: once per character part (both feet, legs, HumanoidRootPart) and repeatedly as contacts change, all before Destroy fully takes effect. Several events are already queued in the same frame, and each one gives 10 coins. Fix: add a debounce or consumed flag that you set before awarding (and do it on the server).

local part = script.Parent
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local taken = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if taken then return end
  local plr = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not plr then return end
  local hum = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  taken = true
  plr.leaderstats.Coins.Value += 10
  part:Destroy()
end)

For respawning coins, use a per-player cooldown table instead of Destroy.
B2: With StreamingEnabled the client only has the instances near the player. Distant parts of the map (the Hotel door) are not streamed in yet when the LocalScript runs, or they get streamed out later. Direct dot-indexing errors when the child isn't present. Fix 1: wait for it, with a timeout: local door = workspace:WaitForChild('Map'):WaitForChild('Buildings'):WaitForChild('Hotel'):WaitForChild('Door', 10), and handle nil plus later stream-out (door.AncestryChanged / Destroying). Fix 2 (better): tag doors with CollectionService and use GetInstanceAddedSignal('Door') plus GetTagged, connecting Touched when each door streams in and cleaning up on InstanceRemoved. Alternatives: set the Hotel model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic or Persistent (Persistent keeps it always loaded, so use it sparingly), or handle door touches on the server, where everything exists.
B3: Bugs: (1) PurchaseGranted is returned even when the pcall fails, so the player is charged and gets nothing. (2) There is no PurchaseId idempotency, so retried receipts (after an error, timeout or shutdown) grant again, giving double coins. (3) Get then Set is not atomic and races with other writes. Use UpdateAsync. (4) plr can be nil if the player left, and plr.UserId then errors. Use info.PlayerId. (5) The live session data isn't updated, and a later save of the player's session can overwrite this DataStore write. Corrected behavior: if the player isn't in the server, return NotProcessedYet. Then use UpdateAsync on the player's data: if receipts[info.PurchaseId] already exists, change nothing; otherwise add 100 coins and record the PurchaseId (trim old ids). If the update fails, return NotProcessedYet. If it succeeds, update the in-memory profile or leaderstats and return PurchaseGranted. Set ProcessReceipt only once.
B4: Remotes serialize arguments. Metatables and functions are not sent, so the client gets a plain table {Name='Rifle', Ammo=30} without Weapon's methods, and w:Fire is nil. Instance arguments are sent as references, and the client can only resolve instances that exist on its side. ServerStorage never replicates to clients, so the Muzzle reference arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data only, and rebuild the object on the client with a shared class module in ReplicatedStorage, for example local w = Weapon.new(data) or setmetatable(data, Weapon). Put the Muzzle somewhere that replicates (ReplicatedStorage or Workspace) and send that reference, or send an identifier and look it up or clone it on the client. Also avoid mixed or non-string keys and sparse arrays in remote tables.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is the direction vector, and its length is the ray's range. A .Unit vector is 1 stud long, so the ray only reaches 1 stud from the origin and almost never hits. The ray can also start inside the shooter's own character and hit it. Fix: scale the direction to the range and use RaycastParams.

local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * 500 -- or (target - origin) for exact distance
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
B6:
When the last player leaves, or the server shuts down, the server can close before the PlayerRemoving handlers' DataStore calls finish. Async SetAsync calls get cut off, and on shutdown PlayerRemoving may not get a chance to complete at all. Standard fix: use game:BindToClose to save every remaining player and wait for those saves to finish (you get about 30 seconds). Run them in parallel with task.spawn, then wait until all are done. Make saving idempotent so a player saved in both PlayerRemoving and BindToClose isn't double-handled (track a saving or saved flag). Use UpdateAsync with pcall and retries instead of a blind SetAsync, and keep periodic autosaves so a crash loses little. In Studio, the BindToClose saves often don't run reliably.

game:BindToClose(function()
  local pending = 0
  for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do pending += 1; task.spawn(function() save(p); pending -= 1 end) end
  while pending > 0 do task.wait() end
end)

local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local UseAbility = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage').Remotes.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse: {[Player]: number} = {}

UseAbility.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, ...)
  local now = os.clock()
  local t = lastUse[player]
  if t and now - t < COOLDOWN then return end -- spam ignored silently
  lastUse[player] = now
  local char = player.Character
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  -- validate any args here, then run the ability on the server
  doAbility(player)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
  lastUse[player] = nil -- no leak
end)

The server-side os.clock timestamp is authoritative, and the client cooldown is only cosmetic. Set the timestamp before any yields so spam within the same window can't slip through.
B8:
local MPS = game:GetService('MarketplaceService')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local store = game:GetService('DataStoreService'):GetDataStore('PlayerData')
local PRODUCT_GEMS100 = 123456

local handlers = {
  [PRODUCT_GEMS100] = function(data) data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + 100 end,
}

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local handler = handlers[info.ProductId]
  if not handler then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end

  local ok, result = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, 'u_' .. info.PlayerId, function(data)
    data = data or {Gems = 0, Receipts = {}}
    data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
    if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return data end -- already granted
    handler(data)
    data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time()
    return data
  end)
  if not ok then
    warn('Receipt failed: ', result)
    return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
  end
  local gems = player:FindFirstChild('leaderstats') and player.leaderstats:FindFirstChild('Gems')
  if gems then gems.Value = result.Gems end -- sync live view
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end

Assign it once. Prune old Receipts entries. If you use a session-cached profile, apply the grant to the profile and save it, rather than writing the key behind the profile's back.
B9:
local TweenService = game:GetService('TweenService')
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local SHOWN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local HIDDEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
local current

local function open()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  menu.Position = HIDDEN
  menu.Visible = true
  current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = SHOWN})
  current:Play()
end

local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local tw = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = HIDDEN})
  current = tw
  tw.Completed:Once(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == tw then
      menu.Visible = false
    end
  end)
  tw:Play()
end

(menu.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5) for centering.) The Completed state check stops a cancelled close from hiding a menu that was reopened.
B10:
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local MAX_RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20

local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= 'Vector3' then return end
  if targetPos ~= targetPos then return end -- NaN guard
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild('Head')
  local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end

  local origin = head.Position
  local offset = targetPos - origin
  if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
  local dir = offset.Unit * MAX_RANGE

  local params = RaycastParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}

  local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass('Model')
  local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
  if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
    hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
  end
end

When this is called from a remote, also rate-limit by fire rate and check line of sight on the server.
B11:
local CollectionService = game:GetService('CollectionService')
local TAG = 'KillBrick'
local conns: {[Instance]: RBXScriptConnection} = {}

local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA('BasePart') or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local hum = hit.Parent and hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
    if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum.Health = 0 end
  end)
end

local function onRemoved(part)
  local c = conns[part]
  if c then c:Disconnect(); conns[part] = nil end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do onAdded(p) end

InstanceRemoved also fires when a tagged part is destroyed, so the table doesn't leak.
B12:
local TeleportService = game:GetService('TeleportService')
local MAX_ATTEMPTS, RETRY_DELAY = 3, 2

local function safeTeleport(placeId: number, players: {Player}, teleportData: any?)
  local options = Instance.new('TeleportOptions')
  if teleportData ~= nil then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
  local ok, result
  for attempt = 1, MAX_ATTEMPTS do
    ok, result = pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, players, options)
    if ok then return true, result end
    warn('Teleport attempt', attempt, 'failed:', result)
    task.wait(RETRY_DELAY * attempt)
  end
  return false, result
end

-- Failures after the call returned are reported here
TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed:Connect(function(player, result, message, placeId, options)
  if result == Enum.TeleportResult.IsTeleporting then return end
  warn('TeleportInitFailed', player, result, message)
  task.wait(RETRY_DELAY)
  if player.Parent then
    pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, {player}, options)
  end
end)

return safeTeleport

In production, cap the retries made from TeleportInitFailed per player (track the attempt count) to avoid loops. Teleport data is client-visible, so don't put anything trusted in it.
B13: (a) Purchase: the client sends a request through a RemoteEvent, BuyItem(itemId), or a RemoteFunction (client to server) if the UI needs an immediate success or failure answer. The server owns the coin balance and prices, validates the item, price and balance, deducts and grants. The client never sends a price or balance. (b) Counter update: replicate the state from the server to the client, either with a leaderstats or Attribute/IntValue on the player that the client watches (GetAttributeChangedSignal or .Changed), or with a server-to-client RemoteEvent (FireClient) carrying the new balance. Why not RemoteFunction:InvokeClient: the server would yield waiting for the client. An exploiter can make it never return (the server thread hangs forever), error, or return garbage, and if the player leaves mid-invoke it errors. It is also unnecessary, since the server doesn't need a reply for a UI update. Use FireClient or replicated values.
B14: Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData, read with Player:GetJoinData().TeleportData on the server) is fast and free but travels through the client. It can be read and tampered with by exploiters, isn't guaranteed to arrive, and has size limits. It is fine for non-authoritative things like the chosen map, party id, or a cosmetic loadout preference that you re-validate. DataStores are authoritative and persistent but slower, have request limits and eventual cross-server consistency, and need session locking so the lobby's write is finished before the match reads. MemoryStores (SortedMap or HashMap) are fast, server-only and cross-server, with TTL, which makes them good for short-lived handoff state such as match assignment or a loadout reservation, but they are not durable. Choice: keep coins in the DataStore (the player's saved profile with a session lock). The lobby saves and releases on teleport, and the match loads it. Never trust coins from teleport data. Pass the loadout as an id in teleport data or a MemoryStore entry keyed by userId, and re-validate it on the match server against owned items.
B15: A Script per instance (610 copies): duplicated code that is hard to update, with bugs fixed in one copy only. Each script costs memory and scheduler overhead and startup time. Copies drift apart, and you can't share state or configuration easily. A tag-driven architecture uses one system module or Script per behavior (DoorSystem, PickupSystem, TurretSystem) under ServerScriptService. Instances get CollectionService tags ('Door', 'Pickup', 'Turret') and per-instance configuration as Attributes. Each system does: for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged(tag) do setup(inst) end, connects GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag) for instances spawned later (cloned from ServerStorage, round resets), and connects GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag) to disconnect connections and clear its per-instance state table. On the client (visuals, prompts), the same pattern handles StreamingEnabled: instances streaming in fire InstanceAdded and streaming out fire InstanceRemoved, so client systems set up and tear down automatically. Keep the authority (damage, pickups) on the server. Turrets can share one Heartbeat loop over a set instead of 60 loops.
B16: Give network ownership of the car's assembly to the driver: on seat occupancy, call vehicle.PrimaryPart:SetNetworkOwner(player) on the server (and SetNetworkOwner(nil) or automatic when they leave). That gives responsive, lag-free physics for the driver, and server ownership would feel laggy. The risk: the owning client simulates the physics and the server accepts it, so an exploiter can teleport the car, speed-hack, fly, noclip, or fling other players and parts it touches. The server must still validate: speed and acceleration caps and position deltas between frames (teleport detection, with a rubber band or reclaiming ownership if exceeded); checkpoint order and lap or finish times (detect checkpoints on the server, enforce minimum plausible times); that the car stays in bounds and isn't flying; that only the seated driver can own or control it; and all rewards and results on the server. Don't trust remote-reported positions or times. Never give ownership of unanchored world parts unnecessarily.
B17: Use UnreliableRemoteEvent for high-frequency, latest-value-wins data like aim direction and position. Also cut the rate (send only on change, quantize, 10-20 Hz) and let the server interpolate. Its constraints: delivery and order are not guaranteed, packets can be dropped or arrive out of order, and payload size is limited (about 1 KB per call; larger payloads are dropped). Handling: include a sequence number or timestamp and ignore older-than-latest packets. Make each message a full snapshot, not a delta, so drops don't matter. Keep the payload small (compact the numbers, maybe use a buffer). Keep reliable RemoteEvents for important one-off events (fire, hit claims, state changes). Validate on the server as usual: rate-limit, sanity-check positions and angles, never trust the client. Note that the server already replicates the character's position via physics, so you often only need to send the aim.
B18: Split the NPCs across Actors. Put each NPC (or a batch of about 10-25) under an Actor with its own Script. In that script, connect RunService.Heartbeat with ConnectParallel (or call task.desynchronize()) to run the raycasts and path scoring in parallel. Raycasts and spatial queries are safe in parallel. Write results into actor-local tables, then call task.synchronize() (or use SharedTable or messages) to apply changes such as setting CFrames, Humanoid:MoveTo, or firing events in the serial phase. Limitations: in the parallel phase most instance writes (property sets, creating or destroying instances) are disallowed and only thread-safe APIs work. Scripts in different Actors don't share Lua state, so communicate through Actor:SendMessage, BindToMessageParallel or SharedTable (copying costs). PathfindingService:ComputeAsync is not parallel-safe and yields, so run pathing less often (stagger it, cache paths) in serial or a few per frame. Keep each actor's work coarse, not one actor per tiny task, because there is scheduling and sync overhead. Measure in the MicroProfiler. Also reduce work: stagger NPC updates across frames, use LOD for far NPCs, and avoid per-frame pathing.
B19: Set Workspace.StreamingEnabled = true. Keep the defaults to start: StreamingMinRadius 64, StreamingTargetRadius 1024, and for mobile memory consider a lower target, such as 256-512 for dense maps. Use StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic (or Default) so content streams out under memory pressure, and StreamingIntegrityMode = Default or PauseOutsideLoadedArea so players don't fall into unloaded areas. Per model: ModelStreamingMode = Atomic for models that must load as a whole (doors, vehicles, NPC rigs), Persistent only for the few things that must always exist (keep these minimal), and LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh for large distant landmarks. Scripts: client code can't assume anything far away exists. Replace direct indexing with WaitForChild (with timeouts) or, better, CollectionService tags with GetInstanceAddedSignal/InstanceRemoved to set up and tear down. Handle instances disappearing (stream-out), and use Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleporting a player or moving the camera far away. Server scripts are unaffected because the server has everything. Test with Studio's streaming emulation and on low-memory devices.
B20: Saving every 5 s for 80 players is about 960 writes per minute, plus the per-key limit (you can't write the same key more often than about once every 6 s). The write budget is about 60 + 10 x players per minute, roughly 860 per minute per server here, so requests queue. When a key's queue fills, newer requests are dropped (error 302, 'queue is full'), and saves are lost or arrive out of order. SetAsync also blindly overwrites. Better design: keep data in memory (a session cache, with a session lock). Autosave each player every 60-120 s (or staggered, only when dirty). Save on PlayerRemoving and in BindToClose. Use UpdateAsync with pcall, retry with backoff, and check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before writing. Never write more often than the per-key rate. For critical events (purchases), save once immediately, not on a loop. A library like ProfileStore already does this.
B21: Enable it in Studio under File > Studio Settings (or the Assistant/AI settings, 'Enable Studio as MCP server'). In newer builds it is a toggle in the Assistant or MCP settings panel. Then point the external client at it (for example claude mcp add with the Studio MCP command or URL). Tools it exposes include: run or execute Luau code in Studio (execute_luau / run_code); script search, read and grep (script_search, script_read, script_grep); multi-edit of scripts (multi_edit); game tree search and instance inspection (search_game_tree, inspect_instance); insert asset or model from the Creator Store (insert_asset, search_asset); start and stop playtests (start_stop_play); get console or output logs (get_console_output); get Studio state; screen capture; and simulated keyboard, mouse and character navigation input during playtests. Generation tools (mesh, material, texture) may also be exposed.
B22: The Input Action System has three core instances. InputContext is a group of actions that can be enabled or disabled together, with a Priority and a Sink option. InputAction is an abstract action (for example Jump or Sprint) with a Type (Bool, Direction1D, Direction2D, ViewportPosition and so on). InputBinding sits under an action and maps a physical input to it: KeyCode (keyboard or gamepad), UIButton (a touch or GUI button), or composite directional keys (Up/Down/Left/Right). A press is signalled by the action's events: Pressed and Released for Bool actions, and StateChanged(newState) for any type, with InputAction:GetState() to poll. The action fires regardless of device, so one handler covers keyboard, gamepad and touch. Menu precedence: put the menu's actions in their own InputContext with a higher Priority than the default player scripts' (gameplay) context, and set Sink = true so inputs bound in the menu context are consumed and don't reach lower-priority contexts (character movement or jump). Enable it when the menu opens and disable it on close (InputContext.Enabled).
B23: UI Styling is a CSS-like system for GuiObjects. Main instances: StyleSheet (holds rules), StyleRule (a Selector string such as 'TextButton', '.Primary' for tags, '#Name', or pseudo-states like ':hover', plus property values set with SetProperty or SetProperties; rules can nest and have Priority), StyleLink (placed under a ScreenGui or other root and links it to a StyleSheet), and StyleDerive (lets a StyleSheet inherit rules from another sheet, for themes). Styles reach the UI by linking: a StyleLink under the ScreenGui points at a StyleSheet, usually in ReplicatedStorage, and every descendant matching a rule's selector gets the rule's properties. Class selectors use CollectionService tags on the GUI objects. Specificity and priority resolve conflicts, and explicitly set properties override styled ones. Tokens are values shared via attributes on the StyleSheet (for example a PrimaryColor attribute), referenced in a rule as '$PrimaryColor'. Changing the attribute (or swapping to a derived theme sheet) updates every rule that uses it.
B24: The check uses facial age estimation: the user takes a short video selfie in the app, processed by a vendor (Persona), and the images are deleted after processing. ID verification is an option for ages 13+. Without a check, chat is unavailable. Age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, and 21+. Restriction: users can only chat with users in their own age group and the adjacent groups (for example 13-15 can chat with 9-12, 13-15 and 16-17), not with much older or younger users. Under-9s have chat off by default unless a parent enables it after the check. Trusted Connections (verified real-life contacts) can chat across groups. Rollout: voluntary in late 2025, then required in some countries (Australia, NZ, Netherlands) from December 2025, then globally from early January 2026.
